title: Global Markets Brief — 23 Nov 2026
intro: Global markets open under intense downward pressure as Wall Street's worst week since 2020 bleeds into a severe risk-off European session. The VIX surges 26.20% to 35.89 alongside deep tech liquidations and escalating geopolitical tensions in the Middle East.

sections.heading: 🌍 Macro tone
sections.content: The macro environment is aggressively risk-off, driven by a brutal tech sector downturn colliding with Anthropic's record IPO and fresh geopolitical supply shocks. Safe havens rally hard as gold climbs 3.06% to 3,622.80 and US Treasury yields drop sharply across the curve.

sections.heading: 🛢 Oil desk
sections.content: WTI trades down 0.40% at 83.08 while Brent falls 3.22% to 89.59, bringing the Brent-WTI spread to 6.51. Crude markets are pressured by slowing global growth and profit-taking, despite Yemen's Houthis claiming attacks on a Saudi oil refinery.

sections.heading: Cross-asset read
sections.content: US 10-year yields tumble 14.0bp to 4.912% and DXY dips 0.19% to 103.61 as equities suffer broad-based losses led by a 5.61% plunge in the Nasdaq 100 to 25,029. Precious metals outperform significantly, with silver jumping 3.52% to 42.48 amid the flight to safety.

sections.heading: Potential scenarios
sections.content:
- *▲ Bullish · Gold — above 3,650.00 opens 3,800.00 · invalid below 3,580.00*
Safe-haven demand surges as equity liquidations and geopolitical tensions drive strong inflows into precious metals.
- *▼ Bearish · Nasdaq 100 — below 24,800 opens 23,500 · invalid above 25,500*
Heavy tech sector selling deepens following the worst weekly performance on Wall Street since 2020.
- *▼ Bearish · DAX — below 24,500 opens 23,500 · invalid above 25,200*
European indices slump in sympathy with global risk-off sentiment ahead of key regional flash manufacturing PMIs.

sections.heading: Key risks
sections.content:
- Escalating Middle Eastern conflict following Houthi attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure.
- Potential contagion from the severe ongoing tech sector liquidity crunch and growth slowdown.
